text:
on giving advice - Seneca with another perfect metaphor for the correct tone and attitude: "...discussing troubles which concern us both, sharing remedies, as if we were lying ill in the same hospital."

--

Q: “What,” say you, “are you giving me advice? Indeed, have you already advised yourself, already corrected your own faults? Is this the reason why you have leisure to reform other men?”

A: "I am, however, discussing with you troubles which concern us both, and sharing the remedy with you, just as if we were lying ill in the same hospital. Listen to me, therefore, as you would if I were talking to myself. I am admitting you to my inmost thoughts, and am having it out with myself, merely making use of you as my pretext."
